'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[2021 Maiduguri rocket attacks]]
***[[Boko Haram]] militants fire a series of [[rocket]]s in [[Maiduguri]], [[Borno State|Borno]], [[Nigeria]], killing 10 civilians and wounding others. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-56184033 (BBC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Africanization]]
**The [[South Africa]]n city of [[Port Elizabeth]] is formally renamed "Gqeberha" ({{IPA|xh|ᶢǃʱɛ̀ɓéːxà|}}), the [[Xhosa people|Xhosa]] name for the Baakens River which flows through the city. Port Elizabeth International Airport is also renamed [[Chief Dawid Stuurman International Airport]], after [[David Stuurman]]. These name changes are part of a wider campaign to remove colonial and [[apartheid]]-era names in the [[Eastern Cape]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-56182349 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****The [[Cabinet of Jordan|cabinet]] extends the curfew to 10:00 p.m., and orders all businesses to close at 9:00 p.m. local time beginning tomorrow due to the spread of the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant. The cabinet also re-imposes a Friday [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-jordan-mobility/jordan-extends-night-curfew-after-wide-spread-of-british-virus-strain-idUSL8N2KU7W7 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] and [[Ministry of Health (Malaysia)|Director-General of Health]] [[Noor Hisham Abdullah]] receive their first doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] as the country officially begins its national immunisation programme. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/02/24/muhyiddin-receives-first-dose-of-covid-19-vaccine (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] lifts their [[COVID-19]]-related restrictions, allowing indoor dining and wedding ceremonies to resume on March 15. Time limits for shopping centres, markets, and amusement parks are also lifted. [https://www.geo.tv/latest/336764-ncoc-loosens-coronavirus-restrictions-starting-march-15 (Geo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] receives their first shipment of 200,000 doses of the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] vaccines. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2073735/first-covid-19-vaccine-arrives (''Bangkok Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] receives their first shipment of 117,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine from [[South Korea]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/vietnam-first-batch-aztrazeneca-covid-19-vaccine-south-korea-14270254 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****The [[Government of Denmark|government]] announces the easing of national COVID-19 restrictions, with shops reopening on March 1. Schools in some areas will also reopen on March 1, but classes will be at 50% capacity. [https://www.thelocal.dk/20210224/denmark-announces-easing-of-covid-19-restrictions-limited-opening-of-schools-and-shops/ (''The Local Denmark'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[Minister of Health (France)|Health Minister]] [[Olivier Véran]] announces that the [[Government of France|government]] will impose a weekend lockdown in [[Dunkirk]] beginning this weekend due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 infections. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210224-france-puts-dunkirk-area-under-lockdown-amid-alarming-covid-19-situation (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]], [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
****The [[Poland|Polish]] [[Ministry of Health (Poland)|Health Ministry]] bans the use of scarves, [[bandana]]s, and [[face shield]]s and requires people to only wear [[surgical mask]]s as of February 27 due to the spread of variants of SARS-CoV-2. [https://polandin.com/52474775/covering-mouth-nose-acceptable-only-with-protective-mask-health-min (Poland In)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]
****The [[Government of Switzerland|government]] announces that it will allow non-essential shops, museums and outdoor sporting facilities to reopen on March 1 as part of an easing of [[social distancing]] restrictions. In addition, outdoor gatherings up to 15 people will also be allowed. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-24/switzerland-eases-lockdown-by-reopening-shops-and-museums (Bloomberg)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
****[[Egypt]] grants emergency use authorization for [[Russia]]'s [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine. [https://www.prnewswire.com/ae/news-releases/rdif-egypt-grants-emergency-use-authorization-for-sputnik-v-301234570.html (PR Newswire)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ghana]]
****[[Ghana]] becomes the first country in the world to receive vaccines distributed through the [[COVAX]] initiative, with 600,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/covax-ghana-astrazeneca-vaccine/2021/02/24/558d31bc-7617-11eb-9489-8f7dacd51e75_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alaska]]
****[[Alaska]] [[Governor of Alaska|governor]] [[Mike Dunleavy (politician)|Mike Dunleavy]] tests positive for COVID-19 following a brief period of isolation after suspected exposure. [https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/540398-alaska-governor-tests-positive-for-covid-19?amp (''The Hill'')]
****Alaska reports their first case of the [[Lineage P.1]] variant first detected in [[Brazil]] in a person from [[Anchorage]] with no known travel history. [https://apnews.com/article/alaska-anchorage-coronavirus-pandemic-a648320ae0d9621888fe3f53efdab8b7 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[California]] surpasses 50,000 deaths of COVID-19, becoming the first [[U.S. state]] to do so. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/feb/25/california-coronavirus-death-toll-covid-19-50000 (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Idaho]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****[[Idaho]] reports their first case of the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant in a person from [[Ada County, Idaho|Ada County]]. [https://www.idahopress.com/coronavirus/uk-variant-of-covid-19-confirmed-in-ada-county-woman/article_72bb2990-83c7-519e-8cf1-d008dd0c1274.html (''Idaho Press'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Carolina]]
****[[North Carolina]] [[Governor of North Carolina|governor]] [[Roy Cooper]] announces that some [[stay-at-home]] and curfew restrictions will be lifted on February 26, such as allowing bars to reopen indoors, increasing the number of people in gatherings, and extending the alcohol sale cutoff to 11:00 p.m. [https://www.newsobserver.com/news/coronavirus/article249467495.html (''The News & Observer'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
****[[Mayor of Washington D.C.]] [[Muriel Bowser]]'s sister, Merica Bowser, dies from COVID-19 as the city surpasses 1,000 total deaths. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2021/02/24/dc-mayor-bowsers-sister-dies-covid-19-city-passes-1-000-deaths/6809594002/ (''USA Today'')]
***[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Johnson & Johnson]]'s single-shot [[Ad26.COV2.S|COVID-19 vaccine candidate]] meets the standards for [[Emergency Use Authorization|emergency use authorization]], according to analysis from a committee within the [[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]], though formal authorization will not be determined until February 26. The vaccine is 66% effective in combating the virus and can be stored in normal refrigerators. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/02/23/health/johnson--johnson-covid-19-vaccine-fda-committee/index.html (CNN)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]], [[501.V2 variant]]
***[[Moderna]] announces that they will ship their [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine candidate]] for testing against the 501.V2 variant that originated in [[South Africa]]. [https://time.com/5942148/moderna-vaccine-covid-19-variant/ (''Time'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Nicolás Maduro]]'s [[government of Venezuela|government]] declares [[European Union]] [[Ambassador]] to [[Venezuela]] [[Isabel Brilhante Pedrosa]] a ''persona non grata'' and gives her 72 hours to leave the country following new sanctions by the EU against 19 Venezuelan officials. [https://www.elmundo.es/internacional/2021/02/24/60367c18fdddff07178b45d6.html (''El Mundo'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Assassination of Luca Attanasio]]
**[[Prime Minister of Italy|Italian Prime Minister]] [[Mario Draghi]] asks the [[United Nations]] and the [[World Food Programme|UN World Food Programme]] to open an investigation into the attack that killed Italian ambassador [[Luca Attanasio]] and two other people. [https://apnews.com/article/world-news-italy-luigi-di-maio-rome-united-nations-41596deaa751c68b3a3245e96a91c28d (AP)]
*[[Drug policy of Germany]]
**Authorities in [[Germany]] and [[Belgium]] seize more than {{convert|23,000|kg|lb}} of [[cocaine]], worth billions of dollars, in an international operation that resulted in one arrest. Authorities consider this to be the largest amount of cocaine ever seized in [[Europe]]. The containers came on a ship from [[Paraguay]], via [[Tangier]] and [[Rotterdam]], the police said. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/02/24/europe/cocaine-bust-grm-intl-scli/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Philippine drug war]], [[2021 PNP-PDEA shootout|PNP–PDEA shootout]]
**A mishandled [[sting operation]] between the [[Philippine National Police|national police]] and the country's [[Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency|drug enforcement agency]] in [[Quezon City]] results in the deaths of two police officers following a shootout between the two parties. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/02/25/asia/philippines-police-drug-bust-intl-hnk-scli/index.html (CNN)]

'''Science and technology'''
*Scientists discover ''[[Dzharatitanis kingi]]'', a [[Diplodocus]]-like dinosaur fossil, in [[Uzbekistan]]. It is the first dinosaur of its kind to be discovered in [[Asia]]. [https://www.newscientist.com/article/2269125-diplodocus-like-fossil-in-uzbekistan-hints-asia-was-a-dinosaur-hub/ (''New Scientist'')]
